title: File Text Replacement
domain: Safe original-path replacement of a file that may be larger than the managed heap.
description: Complete REBOL Cookbook recipe 0004: read an existing file, replace the first occurrence of a byte sequence, and atomically replace the original path. The host supplies general asynchronous filesystem operations; the replacement algorithm is Glon. Source and intermediate temporary data are streamed in bounded chunks.
attribution: Original REBOL 2 Cookbook recipe 'Replace Text in a File' by Carl Sassenrath (archived recipe linked in the reference source pane). The Glon implementation and reusable vocabulary are original for this challenge.
reference: REBOL replace changes only the first occurrence and the original program writes the result back to the same path. The cases use independently generated expected bytes from Python bytes.replace(old, new, 1), including failure cases that must leave the original unchanged.
history: Previous published result: partial in-memory implementation. The pinned CLI had no file read/write vocabulary, so the original file round trip was not reproduced; six in-memory cases passed.

This result: the optional file module is built with MODULES=file, and a protocol-v2 temp/commit/discard service plus reusable file/replace-first vocabulary complete the original-path operation. The previous partial result is superseded but retained here and in Git history.

performance.note: Measured in the engineering integration worktree on WSL2 with the native -O0 build. Wall times are host-load sensitive; expected bytes and temp cleanup were verified. Managed heap capacity is 7,232 cells.

known_limitations: POSIX-only optional file backend; no WASM, Windows or embedded file backend.
Atomic replacement is process-level, not power-loss durable: no file or directory fsync is performed.
Ownership, group, ACLs, xattrs and timestamps are not preserved; source permission bits are.
A symlink final component is rejected. Other hard links keep the old content after replacement.
Concurrent source modification is detected best-effort from device/inode/size/mtime/mode; there is no locking or content hash.
Cancellation is cooperative at request boundaries; a commit already executing may complete atomically.
A forcibly killed process can leave a .glon-tmp-* file; normal failure/cleanup paths remove it.
The managed heap is fixed at 7,232 cells; GC time grows with file size even though live memory stays bounded.
Full ./s1 still stalls in the documented long simulation tests; the non-simulation runner passes. WASM tests were not run because emcc was unavailable.

reference_implementation.title: Replace Text in a File — original REBOL 2 Cookbook program
reference_implementation.attribution: Author: Carl Sassenrath. REBOL Cookbook, recipe 0004, 'Replace Text in a File'.
reference_implementation.notes: Reads %doc.txt, replaces the first occurrence of "web" with "rebol", and writes the modified contents back to %doc.txt.

layers.rebol: REBOL 2 provides its own runtime and series/file facilities. This comparison does not assert which of read, replace or write are core primitives.
layers.glon: Frozen S1 has seven primitives and the R0 evaluator has no file or replace primitive. The host file service moves bytes and performs general temp/commit/discard operations; replacement semantics are library code.
layers.note: Different substrate layers; no source-size comparison.

layers.rebol: replace is a mezzanine in Oldes' Rebol 3 at src/mezz/mezz-series.reb:129. This does not establish the exact implementation or provenance of REBOL 2's replace.
layers.glon: s/replace-first, stream/replace-first-to and file/replace-first are reusable Glon library code. file/replace-first composes first-occurrence replacement with same-directory temporary output and atomic commit. MASM-1 search and MASM-2 request encoding are loaded from vendored libraries.

layers.rebol: The Cookbook application is four lines: read a file, call the existing replace mezzanine, and write the same file.
layers.glon: cookbook/replace-first invokes the reusable file/replace-first operation with the Cookbook path and strings, plus honest asynchronous success/failure callbacks.
layers.note: Both listings are application code. The Glon application composes a reusable library; it does not reproduce REBOL syntax or mutate immutable strings.

implementation_comparison.notice: Source sizes are factual metadata labelled by abstraction layer. The REBOL listing uses existing read/replace/write facilities; the Glon listing composes a reusable library and an optional host file service. This is not a concision claim.
